summary: TASK-070 (REQ-104 dead-code/shell-cluster deletion) independent re-review after the r1 repair round. I did not write any of this code. I re-verified the candidate binding myself (all 157 candidate_files sha256 match the working tree, 0 mismatches/missing; 17 modified non-workflow files all inside allowed_paths; package.json/package-lock.json/Cargo.toml/Cargo.lock diff-vs-HEAD empty; all changed files LF; the user's real DB %APPDATA%\com.fluxreader.app\fluxreader.db still sha256 419b118e.../90112 B/mtime 2026-09-19 01:58:09, untouched), independently re-ran three of the four gates (cargo test exit 0 = 27 suites / 177 passed / 0 failed / 9 ignored, matching the record and the r1 candidate; npm run lint exit 0 = 0 warnings/0 errors; npm run test:frontend exit 0 = 26/26 + 277/277 = 303/303), read the recorded build log and re-ran its typecheck half tsc -b (exit 0), and used targeted mutation experiments (each file restored byte-identically and re-hashed afterwards) to judge whether the adapted assertions still have teeth. F1 and F2 are substantively fixed: sync/mod.rs no longer claims a failure-triggered backend fallback, ingestion.rs now describes backoff and admits the old claim was untrue, and I independently confirmed the factual core (fetch_failed has no consuming reader in Rust; source='miniflux' is written only at sync/entries.rs:214 from 'remote entry matched nothing AND remote feed already bound', which is unrelated to fetch failure). F3 is fixed: the unreachable ac=='subscribe' mock arm is gone, no assertion lost its object (no test ever asserted that path at HEAD; subscribed_urls is still written by the quickadd branch at mock_greader.rs:774 and still read by account_lifecycle_e2e.rs:491 and sync_gap_repro_e2e.rs:1185; subscription_edits is still recorded before the match at mock_greader.rs:799). The repair is not clean, however, and I am reporting FAIL for two comment-honesty defects in the deliverable surface: (1) the replacement F1 sentence in sync/mod.rs:8 over-claims in the opposite direction - 'feeds.fetch_failed only drives exponential-backoff retry' is false twice over (the flag also drives the frontend failure badge via FeedRow -> list_feeds -> api.ts fetchFailed -> Sidebar.tsx:240, and the backoff itself is driven by fail_count/next_retry_at, not by fetch_failed); (2) the same false 'Miniflux fallback triggered by direct-fetch failure' claim that F1/F2 removed elsewhere is still present in src-tauri/tests/sync_e2e.rs:3 and :170-171, a file that is in allowed_paths and that this task modified - I disproved its causal claim by mutation (deleting only the set_feed_fetch_state(...,true,...) call leaves the test green and the miniflux entry still ingested; the real trigger is the remote_id binding). The r2 artifact's inventory of remaining stale wording omits this in-scope file. Everything else checks out: no new dead_code/unused warnings (normalized warning multisets of baseline vs r1 vs r2 cargo_test.stderr are identical: 1 linker warning + 3 'multiple methods are never used' + 1 'set_fail_edit_tag...' + 8 per-test-target duplicates), zero residue of fallback_entries / api.syncNow / STATE_FILE_NAME, per-suite result sequences identical to baseline and to r1, 177 test-case names identical to r1 (baseline vs r2 differs only by the documented rename article_id_by_url_uses_normalized_match -> normalized_url_match_maps_same_article), no new dependencies, and the renamed/adapted assertions still fail under mutation except where the insensitivity pre-dates this task. Performance is genuinely not applicable.
findings: N1 (medium, requirements+maintainability, src-tauri/src/sync/mod.rs:8) - the F1 replacement sentence over-claims: 'feeds.fetch_failed 只驱动指数退避重试' is inaccurate in two directions. (a) The flag is NOT only a retry input: it is part of FeedRow (src-tauri/src/db/feeds.rs:16, serialized), returned by the list_feeds command (src-tauri/src/commands/folders.rs:103-105, registered in src-tauri/src/lib.rs:230), typed in src/lib/api.ts:57, mapped at src/lib/api.ts:534 to fetchFailed, and consumed by the UI failure badge at src/components/Sidebar.tsx:240-247 ('最近抓取失败，点击重试'). (b) The exponential backoff is not driven by fetch_failed at all: set_feed_fetch_state writes fail_count/next_retry_at and the retry window is decided by feeds_due_for_refresh via next_retry_at (src-tauri/src/db/feeds.rs:130-134 and :152-156); fetch_failed itself is a pure marker. The header's real point (no failure-triggered backend fallback path exists) is correct and verified, but the fix replaced one untrue claim with another. Suggested wording: state that fetch_failed is a failure marker consumed only by the UI today, that backoff is driven by fail_count/next_retry_at, and that no sync-path fallback reads it.

N2 (low-medium, requirements+maintainability, src-tauri/tests/sync_e2e.rs:3 and :170-171) - the same 'direct-fetch failure triggers a Miniflux fallback' claim that F1/F2 removed from the production headers survives, unfixed, inside an in-scope file that this task already modified. Line 3 of the module header says the suite covers '直连失败源的兜底拉取（source='miniflux'）' and line 170 says '③ 兜底：直连失败的源从 Miniflux 拉条目' with line 171 '把 local_feed 标记为直连失败 + 绑定远端 feed'. I disproved the causal claim experimentally: removing only the db::set_feed_fetch_state(&conn, local_feed_id, true, Some("connection refused"), None, None) call (nothing else changed) still leaves the suite green and still ingests the remote-only entry as source='miniflux' - the effective trigger is the feed's remote_id binding plus an unmatched remote entry, exactly as F1 established. The r2 artifact's 'NOT CHANGED' list (src/types.ts:44/:70, tests/staged_refresh_e2e.rs:195, tests/sync_phases_e2e.rs:246) justifies itself with 'outside this task's allowed_paths', but src-tauri/tests/sync_e2e.rs IS in allowed_paths and is in the task's own diff, so this file was simply missed. The fix is comment-only; the assertions themselves (the source='miniflux' and title-contains-'Fallback' checks) are still valid and should stay, only the failure-trigger framing should be corrected.

review_checks.analysis: Item-by-item against the deletion inventory and the seven acceptance criteria, verified independently rather than from the author's narrative. Candidate binding: recomputed sha256 for all 157 candidate_files - 157/157 match, 0 mismatched, 0 missing. Only 17 non-.workflow-kit paths are modified and every one is inside allowed_paths; no untracked files outside .workflow-kit. (1) Zero-production-call: verified against HEAD with git grep, not just the worktree. At HEAD, feeds_fetch_failed / feeds_origin_remote / feeds_fetch_failed_bound appear only as definitions plus the db.rs pub use; article_matches_remote_feed / article_id_by_url / set_folder_remote_id appear only as definitions, the db.rs re-export and three test files; article_has_pending_sync / feed_by_remote_id are not referenced by anything but their own definitions/comments; fallback_entries has no increment anywhere (only the mutually-copying assignments at phases.rs:90 and commands/sync.rs:269); api.syncNow has no caller; STATE_FILE_NAME has no reference; AiEvent::Error is constructed only by its own test. So all nine deletions were genuinely dead BEFORE the change - no caller was deleted to manufacture 'deadness', i.e. no scope creep of that kind. The db.rs re-export set shrank from 106 to 98 names and the 8 removed names are exactly the 8 deleted functions (no accidental export loss, nothing new added). The deletions are reflected consistently across Rust and TypeScript. (2) Four gates green: cargo test exit 0 (27 suites, 177/0/9), lint exit 0 (0 warnings/0 errors), frontend exit 0 (303/303) - all independently re-run by me and matching the recorded RUN-dafb37cd; build not re-run per instruction, but I read the raw build log (exit 0) and independently re-ran its typecheck half tsc -b (exit 0). (3) Zero residue: git grep over src, src-tauri/src and tools for fallback_entries, fallbackEntries, syncNow and STATE_FILE_NAME returns empty (exit 1) - no string-level leftovers. (4) AiEvent::Error: the delete option was chosen and recorded; the variant and its dedicated serialization assertion are gone, the frontend 'error' branch is intentionally retained as a defensive fallback with an honest comment (src/lib/api.ts:316-320). That branch is still reachable code with a live onError parameter, so no unused-parameter breakage (tsconfig.app.json has noUnusedParameters and tsc -b passes). (5) sync/mod.rs no longer claims the nonexistent Miniflux fallback - the literal criterion is met and I confirmed the replacement text's substance (origin='remote' feeds really are covered by the GReader reading-list pull at sync/greader_pull.rs:38 and the Fever unread/saved collections at sync/fever_pull.rs:52 and :110-127; no failure-triggered fallback exists anywhere). However the remaining clause of that same repaired sentence is itself inaccurate (see finding N1), and the objective-level requirement 'ensure no unfulfilled capability claims' is still unmet in src-tauri/tests/sync_e2e.rs (see finding N2), which is why this area is FAIL rather than PASS. (6) No new dependencies: diff vs HEAD for package.json, package-lock.json, src-tauri/Cargo.toml and src-tauri/Cargo.lock is empty. All 17 changed files are LF-only with a trailing newline; no CRLF anywhere. The user's real database is untouched (sha256 419b118e050a08c204a50603f2d5188d8132fa94d75ea417392fe7e984293550, 90112 bytes, mtime 2026-09-19 01:58:09, i.e. before this candidate's verification). (7) Equivalent coverage for retired tests: the two retired assertions had only dead objects (the permanently-zero fallback_entries print; the never-constructed AiEvent::Error serialization). The three adapted tests were re-verified for teeth by mutation, not by reasoning. No incidental behaviour change found: the only non-deletion edit besides comments is commands/sync.rs now delegating to sync::sync_now, which runs the same feeds_phase -> states_phase(full=true) sequence with the same merge arithmetic (phases.rs:82-92) minus the deleted O(1) field assignment.

I read the actual gate commands and raw outputs and re-ran three gates myself. Recorded numbers are truthful: cargo_test stdout aggregates to exactly 177 passed / 0 failed / 9 ignored over 27 suites, and the per-suite sequence is byte-for-byte the same as the baseline RUN-5380e8e4 and as the r1 candidate RUN-49ba05fc (86/0/0, 0/0/0, 6/0/0, 1/0/0, 8/0/0, 3/0/0, 4/0/0, 14/0/0, 4/0/0, 0/0/3, 0/0/1, 2/0/0, 0/0/3, 0/0/1, 2/0/0, 0/0/0, 3/0/0, 2/0/0, 4/0/0, 1/0/0, 3/0/1, 3/0/0, 7/0/0, 1/0/0, 18/0/0, 5/0/0, 0/0/0). My own run reproduces 27 suites / 177 / 0 / 9 with exit 0. lint stdout is 'Found 0 warnings and 0 errors... 65 files' with exit 0. frontend stdout ends with the three totals 26/26, 277/277 and 303/303 with zero occurrences of 'failed', exit 0. build stdout shows exit 0; I did not re-run it, but tsc -b (its typecheck half) exits 0. Coverage was not silently dropped: the set of 177 test-case names is identical between r1 and r2, and between baseline and r2 it differs by exactly one rename (article_id_by_url_uses_normalized_match -> normalized_url_match_maps_same_article) with zero net disappearance. No new compiler warnings were introduced: normalizing the cargo_test.stderr warning lines (dropping the linker-message noise and collapsing the per-test-target 'generated 1 warning' lines) gives the SAME multiset for baseline, r1 and r2 (1 lib linker warning, 3 'multiple methods are never used', 1 'set_fail_edit_tag/set_fail_item_contents/set_fail_reading_list_ids are never used', plus 8 per-target duplicates); the only textual difference is which test target is credited with the duplicate, which is a scheduling artifact. Do the three adapted tests still protect the same behaviour? I re-verified by mutation (each mutated file backed up first and restored byte-identically, verified by sha256 afterwards). (a) Making sync_match_maps write a None feed component into id_to_mf_pair fails dedup_sync_e2e at cross_feed_remote_entry_cannot_write_state_or_steal_binding (tests/dedup_sync_e2e.rs:247) - the rewritten same-feed matrix genuinely still separates same-feed / cross-feed / unbound / missing, and the added input-completeness assertion (lines 256-261) is real. (b) Removing trailing-slash normalisation from normalize_url fails sync_content_e2e at normalized_url_match_maps_same_article (tests/sync_content_e2e.rs:354, left None vs right Some(1)) - the rewritten test is not a tautology. (c) Removing 'UPDATE folders SET remote_id = NULL' from purge_remote_data does NOT fail account_lifecycle_e2e; I traced why and it is a pre-existing property, not an adaptation regression: purge step 5 deletes the now-empty remote folder row outright, so 'COUNT(*) FROM folders WHERE remote_id IS NOT NULL' is 0 either way, and the HEAD version that used set_folder_remote_id to build the state had exactly the same insensitivity. The adaptation changed the construction from a (dead) helper call to an equivalent SQL write and left the assertion text and semantics untouched, so it did not weaken anything. One honest limitation, not scored as a defect because it pre-dates this task: the production expression at src-tauri/src/sync/entries.rs:82-89 (same_feed_trusted inside merge_remote_status) is not killed by any test - I replaced its comparison with 'true' and the entire suite stayed green. The adapted dedup test's own comment (tests/dedup_sync_e2e.rs:195-196) states plainly that it replicates the production decision to validate the maps inputs rather than calling the production entry point, so this residual gap is disclosed rather than hidden, and the deleted article_matches_remote_feed it replaced was itself dead code that nothing in production called. The adjacent guard in merge_pulled_entry (is_own) IS killed: neutering it fails dual_client_e2e read_intent_flows_both_ways_across_feeds.

For a deletion task I looked specifically for paths where a deleted symbol was still reachable at runtime, including references a symbol grep would miss, plus rare/flagged branches, empty and repeated executions, and data boundaries. (a) String and IPC-level references: the removed frontend method api.syncNow was the only sender of the 'sync_now' invoke name; no source file anywhere still contains the string 'syncNow' or an invoke of 'sync_now', while the Rust command itself remains registered (src-tauri/src/lib.rs:258) and reachable, so nothing that the running app might call has gone missing. The full-sync UI paths go through api.syncPhase -> inv('sync_phase'), which is untouched (src/lib/api.ts:489-491, src/store/slices/sync.ts:79-86, src/components/settings/SyncTab.tsx:92-98). (b) Serialized field names the frontend reads: 'fallback_entries' was removed from both the Rust struct (sync/mod.rs:27-34) and the TypeScript interface (src/lib/api.ts:96-103) and the regression harness mock (tools/frontend-regression.mjs), and no reader remains (grep is empty), so there is no 'reads undefined' path; src/store/syncErrors.ts still consumes only errors. The retained AiEvent tags 'delta' and 'done' are byte-identical, and only the never-emitted 'error' tag was dropped, with the receiver branch kept. (c) Database columns read elsewhere: the deletion removed Rust query helpers, not schema. feeds.fetch_failed still exists (src-tauri/src/db/migrations.rs:33), is still written by set_feed_fetch_state (src-tauri/src/db/feeds.rs:125) and is still read - including by the frontend failure badge via FeedRow -> list_feeds -> api.ts:534 -> Sidebar.tsx:240 - so no UI or migration path was orphaned by removing the three query helpers; migrations and the column definition are untouched, so existing databases remain compatible. (d) Rarely exercised / feature-flagged code: the scheduler's two entry points (scheduled and manual full refresh) both obtain ids through feeds_due_for_refresh / feeds_all_ids, which filter only on origin and due/backoff windows (src-tauri/src/db/feeds.rs:146-168) and never read fetch_failed, so removing the three 'fallback' queries cannot change any automatic or manual fetch path. The nine #[ignore]d live/network tests are unchanged in count (9) and untouched by this diff, so no ignored path was silently activated or broken. (e) Error-handling branches and repeats: the staged refresh failure branch (src-tauri/src/ingestion.rs:485-496) still writes the failure state; the deleted non-staged refresh_feed was never called by the command layer (src-tauri/src/commands/articles.rs:202-209 calls refresh_feed_staged, as do the scheduler and the tests). Deleting the GReaderClient::subscribe / mark_all_read methods removed no error path, since nothing transmitted those verbs any more (grep for .subscribe(/.mark_all_read( is empty; the client only sends ac=unsubscribe at src-tauri/src/greader.rs:510 and ac=edit at :525). (f) Data boundary: all test databases are synthetic temp files, and the user's real database was verified untouched (hash and mtime unchanged, earlier than the verification run). I found no runtime-reachable use of any deleted symbol.

For a deletion task the main deliverable is comment and documentation honesty, so I checked every rewritten comment against the code and looked for remaining contradictions in the touched files. Genuinely fixed and accurate: db/sync_map.rs's block header now describes the superseded per-item queries generically and names the five deleted functions (lines 24-26); the six SyncMatchMaps field docs no longer cross-reference deleted helpers and now state the real semantics ('None 表示未绑定'; id_to_mf_pair described as the input from which production derives same_feed_trusted), which I confirmed against sync_match_maps (lines 62-88) and its consumers (sync/entries.rs:82-89, :118-128); set_feed_remote_id's doc was narrowed to 'feeds' in step with the set_folder_remote_id removal; get_first_folder_id carries a truthful keep-and-hand-off note (its only remaining reference is the in-crate test src-tauri/src/db/sync_extraction_tests.rs, which is outside allowed_paths); commands/ai.rs documents why the variant went away; commands/sync.rs:262-266 explains the de-duplication motive and genuinely collapses two implementations into one (commands::sync_now now delegates to sync::sync_now), which removes a real drift hazard; ingestion.rs:1-8 now says the flag drives backoff and explicitly records that the former 'Miniflux fallback query' claim was untrue and that the two queries were deleted; and mock_greader.rs:829-831 documents the removal of the unreachable arm, with subscribed_urls still recorded by the quickadd branch (line 774) and subscription_edits still recorded before the match (lines 799-802), so no bookkeeping silently vanished. Why FAIL: (i) the F1 replacement sentence at src-tauri/src/sync/mod.rs:8 is inaccurate in the opposite direction - 'feeds.fetch_failed 只驱动指数退避重试' ignores that the same flag is a serialized UI field that drives the sidebar failure badge (db/feeds.rs:16 -> commands/folders.rs:103 -> api.ts:57/:534 -> Sidebar.tsx:240) and misattributes the backoff, which is actually driven by fail_count/next_retry_at (db/feeds.rs:130-134, :152-156); (ii) src-tauri/tests/sync_e2e.rs:3 and :170-171 still assert the exact non-existent capability that F1/F2 were raised to remove, inside an allowed_paths file that this task already edited, and its causal claim is experimentally false (see the two findings). Also recorded without scoring: the r2 artifact's hand-off inventory of remaining stale 'Miniflux fallback' wording justifies itself with 'outside this task's allowed_paths' and lists src/types.ts:44/:70, tests/staged_refresh_e2e.rs:195 and tests/sync_phases_e2e.rs:246; the first two arguments hold for those paths (src/types.ts:44/:70 is genuinely stale - 'fetchFailed ... 失败走 Miniflux 兜底 + 退避重试' - and the allowed_paths entry literally names the nonexistent src/lib/types.ts, which I confirmed does not exist), but the inventory is incomplete because it omits the in-scope sync_e2e.rs sites. Scope discipline otherwise looks right: no new abstraction layers, no cross-layer dependency added, and the merge_remote_status invariant region was left byte-identical.

Not applicable to this change, with a concrete reason rather than an invented benchmark. This is a pure deletion plus one equivalent delegation, and none of it is on a hot path at runtime. (1) Everything deleted had zero call sites, so it never executed: the three Miniflux-fallback queries, the old non-staged ingestion::refresh_feed, GReaderClient::mark_all_read/subscribe, the five per-item queries, STATE_FILE_NAME and api.syncNow. (2) The structure that actually determines sync complexity - the SyncMatchMaps batch pre-fetch - is unchanged in the diff: sync_match_maps still issues the same 5 batch queries and the merge loop still does O(1) HashMap/HashSet lookups (src-tauri/src/db/sync_map.rs:46-122, consumed at src-tauri/src/sync/entries.rs:99-154), so there is no measurable delta in query count or per-entry work. (3) The only executed-code change is commands::sync_now delegating to sync::sync_now: the sequence is still feeds_phase (push_feeds + pull_feeds) followed by states_phase(full=true), with the same error-merge arithmetic (src-tauri/src/sync/phases.rs:82-92); the single removed operation is one O(1) field copy of the deleted fallback_entries counter, which is nanoseconds against network I/O and SQLite work. (4) Removing one enum variant and one frontend method changes no call counts (the method had none) and no runtime dispatch. (5) The task's quality-goal performance targets (ten-thousand-item startup/layout switching, social-layout article loading) belong to REQ-001/003 and are untouched by this deletion surface; no workload, baseline or measurement exists for them here, so I did not fabricate one and I claim no speedup.
